title: War declared; trenches, Pops Foster and fleeing toward Dunkirk
summary: In September 1939 his Swedish girlfriend could not cross the border; a comedian Pops Foster warned him, he found trenches outside, raised money and tried to reach a ship at Dunkirk as the Germans arrived.

story.theme_name: Drafted: musicians in the military and the war years
story.community_name: Drafted: service bands, USO shows and the war years

blocks.x: That night, of August -- was it August or September, I think it was September 2nd, there was a long distance call from Sweden because my Swedish girl was supposed to come down and visit me.

She said, 'I can't get across the frontier, that war has been declared and I can't cross the frontier.' That was it. So I said, well, let them do what they got to do. I wouldn't care less, but the next day, there was a -- I heard

someone calling me.

The fellow was named Pops Foster. He was a comedian and he was an old fellow. He was a comedian and a dancer. and he's hollering Jacques, Jacques -- he had one of them strange voices that could carry but you could hear him.

So, I --
So, he's different from the Pops Foster that --

No, it's not the same one. That's what I wanted to -- and, I went downstairs and he says Man, you'd better get out of here. This is it. And I looked down and they had trenches in front of me. They had trenches and/ every- thing.

I ran upstairs and packed and by the way, she had told me, I'm going to send you a telegram with some money in it and you can come to Sweden. You be away from that war, see. So, I got the money.

Now, but --/ this ship didn't have no room and it was leaving out, and that was the last one going that way. The man says, well, I advise you to go to a place -- go to Dunkirk because the ships are leaving from Dunkirk, going to Denmark and you'll be right.

But there is another place in Belgium, I forget the name of this place, it's right across the bridge from Dunkirk.

So, I said -- and the frontier is closed off see. I was lucky enough to go back and get my -- I said, well, I'll
be in Dunkirk, I might get that ship, even a Dutch ship or a Danish ship.
Got up there and I stayed up there. The Germans come in. They come in there and they stayed there for about -- I mean, they stayed.
